answer: Give every new agent a tiny task cap and a copper-sized refundable bond, then let it grow only by finishing real work. The kernel scheduler hands out cheap micro-tasks first; each completed job, verified by peers, raises the cap, while missed deadlines forfeit the bond. A sybil operator faces an ocean of small bonds and hours of real compute per identity before any of them can touch valuable work, so cloning a thousand agents costs a thousand bonds and a thousand honest work histories, far more than the payout.
